title: Rent vs buy a home — a decision, not a dream
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Buying a home is not automatically better than renting. Owning adds a down payment (10–25% of the price), EMI, stamp duty and registration (a few percent), maintenance, property tax and the cost of being tied to one location, while the rental yield on a home in most Indian cities is only about 2–3% of its value a year. If you rent and invest the money you would have used for the down payment and the EMI-minus-rent difference, you may do as well or better, especially if you may move cities. Buying makes sense when you are settled for 7–10+ years, the EMI is comfortable (total EMIs under about 40% of take-home income), you still keep an emergency fund after the down payment, and you have done a full cost comparison. Use the Rent vs Buy calculator on the Home tab with your own numbers.
summary_hinglish: Ghar kharidna hamesha rent se behtar nahi. Down payment (10-25%), EMI, stamp duty, maintenance sab lagta hai, aur rent yield sirf 2-3% hota hai. 7-10+ saal ek jagah rehna ho, EMI income ke 40% se kam ho aur emergency fund bacha ho tab buy sochna chahiye. Home tab ka Rent vs Buy calculator use karo.
summary_hi: घर खरीदना हमेशा किराये से बेहतर नहीं होता। डाउन पेमेंट (10-25%), EMI, स्टाम्प ड्यूटी और रखरखाव लगता है, और किराया प्रतिफल केवल 2-3% होता है। 7-10+ साल एक जगह रहना हो, EMI आय के 40% से कम हो और आपातकालीन फंड बचा हो तब खरीदना सोचें। होम टैब का रेंट बनाम खरीद कैलकुलेटर इस्तेमाल करें।
